disclaimer: Published typical values and publicly cited standard figures. None of these are measurements of the laboratory generator or a CPRI specification. They never override a measured value or a workbook formula. Confirm against the laboratory nameplate and the applicable standard edition before using them for a real test.

sources.title: An investigation into the relevancy of the wave shape parameters used for lightning impulse tests
sources.excerpt: IEC 60-1 accepted differences: peak +/-3%, front time +/-30%, time to half-value +/-20%. T1 defined as 1.67 times the 30%-90% interval.

sources.title: Nord-IS paper citing IEEE Std 4 and IEC 60060-1 lightning impulse tolerances
sources.excerpt: Standard lightning impulse T1 = 1.2 us +/-30% (0.84-1.56 us) and T2 = 50 us +/-20% (40-60 us).

impulse_windows.front_definition: Time to peak Tp from the actual origin to the crest, not the 30/90 construction.
impulse_windows.conflict_with_workbook: Workbook H13 applies +/-20% to the switching tail (2000-3000 us). Public citations of IEC 60060-1:2010 use +/-60% (1000-4000 us).

sources.title: An Accurate Evaluation of Switching Impulse Voltages for High-Voltage Tests
Reference Switching Impulse Voltage Measuring System Based on Correcting the Voltage Divider Response With Software
sources.excerpt: Standard SI voltage has Tp of 250 us +/-20% and T2 of 2500 us +/-60% per IEC 60060-1:2010.

impulse_windows.front_definition: Switching impulse redefined with a front time; standard switching impulse becomes 170/2500 us. Lightning T1 positive tolerance extended to +100% (2.4 us) for Um > 800 kV.

sources.title: IEC 60060-1:2025 High-voltage test techniques - Part 1
sources.excerpt: Official change list: LI front-time positive tolerance +100% for Um > 800 kV; SI redefined as 170/2500 us with a front-time definition.

source.title: IS/IEC 60071-1 (2006) Insulation co-ordination, Table 3
source.excerpt: Public Indian republication of IEC 60071-1 Table 3, range II, Um = 300 kV.

source.title: IS/IEC 60071-1 (2006) Insulation co-ordination, Table 3
source.excerpt: Public Indian republication of IEC 60071-1 Table 3, range II, Um = 362 kV.

source.title: IS/IEC 60071-1 (2006) Insulation co-ordination, Table 3
source.excerpt: For Um = 420 kV, standard LIWV includes 1050, 1175, 1300 and 1425 kV; SIWV includes 850, 950 and 1050 kV. The workbook's 1425 kV lightning request is one of these listed levels, not a laboratory measurement. Further Um rows should be copied from the same table when a new voltage class arrives; do not interpolate.

test_objects.label: Cap-and-pin disc (self-capacitance of one disc)
test_objects.note: These are per-disc values. A string of n discs is a series connection, so the two-terminal capacitance is roughly C_disc/n plus stray, typically a few picofarads — not n times C_disc. The workbook's 850 pF is a test-circuit load, not this self-capacitance.

sources.title: Experimental, analytical and numerical analysis of voltage distribution along the cap-and-pin insulators
sources.excerpt: Parasite self-capacitance of a disc insulator estimated at about 40 pF.

sources.title: Application of a genetic algorithm for calculating the capacitances on an insulator string
sources.excerpt: Fitted disc capacitances C of 109.2, 149.0 and 130.6 pF on three experimental strings.

test_objects.label: 400 kV cap-and-pin string disc count
test_objects.note: Utility stringing practice for 400 kV single suspension, not a capacitance. Combine with per-disc C only as C/n.

sources.title: Stringing of conductors and earth wire (400 kV disc counts)
sources.excerpt: 400 kV single suspension I-string: 1 x 23 discs; double suspension 2 x 24.

test_objects.label: 400 kV composite long-rod lightning impulse withstand (manufacturer)
test_objects.note: One manufacturer's FXBW-400/160 rating. Not a measured capacitance and not a CPRI value. Structure height 3315 +/-50 mm.

sources.title: 400 kV composite suspension insulator FXBW-400/160
sources.excerpt: Lightning impulse withstand 1425 kV; structure height 3315 +/-50 mm; wet power-frequency 770 kV.

test_objects.label: 400 kV composite station post lightning impulse withstand (manufacturer)
test_objects.note: One manufacturer's station-post rating. No published capacitance was found. Height 4174 +/-50 mm.

sources.title: 400 kV polymer substation insulator
sources.excerpt: Lightning impulse withstand 1550 kV; height 4174 +/-50 mm; IEC 61952.

test_objects.label: 400-420 kV OIP condenser bushing C1
test_objects.note: Nameplate C1 (HV to tap) from published examples. Use the bushing's own nameplate. This is a two-terminal capacitance, unlike a disc string.

sources.title: Condenser bushings condition monitoring, Transformers Magazine Special Edition
sources.excerpt: 420 kV 1600 A OIP bushing C1 = 489 pF; 800 kV 2500 A OIP C1 = 463 pF.

sources.title: Zustandsbewertung betriebsgealterter Hochspannungstransformatordurchfuhrungen (400 kV example)
sources.excerpt: Worked 400 kV transformer bushing example uses a capacitance of 370 pF.

test_objects.label: 400 kV capacitive / damped-capacitive divider HV arm
test_objects.note: Published HV-arm capacitances for laboratory dividers. The workbook's 500 pF sits in this band. Fast pulse dividers can be 6-15 pF and are a different class.

sources.title: Reference switching-impulse measuring system (400 kV modular divider)
sources.excerpt: Three 1200 pF paper-oil modules, 140 kV peak each, stacked for 400 kV.

sources.title: KRISS/NRC comparison of a 400 kV capacitive voltage divider
sources.excerpt: Each 200 kV unit has a high-voltage capacitor CH of nominal 1000 pF.

sources.title: US6456094B2 capacitive divider for millisecond pulses
sources.excerpt: HV capacitor C1 for pulse voltages above 100 kV is typically 6 to 15 pF. Different class from a 400 kV impulse divider.

circuit_typical.label: Marx generator voltage efficiency
circuit_typical.note: Published Marx voltage-efficiency band. The workbook's 0.82 sits inside it. Efficiency is still an operator input, not a derived quantity. One paper suggests keeping C2 below about 15% of erected C1 to stay above 80%.

sources.title: Reconfiguration of 3 MV Marx Generator into a Modern High Efficiency System
sources.excerpt: Intrinsic efficiency approximated as exceeding 93%. To maintain efficiency above 80%, capacitive loads should not exceed 15% of the net series capacitance.

circuit_typical.label: Laboratory impulse-generator stray inductance
circuit_typical.note: Published laboratory-generator inductance bands. The workbook's 18.5 uH is inside the total-circuit band. Measure the actual loop; do not adopt 18.5 uH for a different hall.

sources.title: Reconfiguration of 3 MV Marx Generator into a Modern High Efficiency System
sources.excerpt: Inductance can vary from 10 uH to several hundreds of uH; some multistage generators estimated at 3 uH/stage; external circuit including specimen roughly 1 uH/m. Example calculation uses L = 40 uH.

sources.title: Characterization of Marx Generator (CPRI journal)
sources.excerpt: Ten-stage Marx total inductance 2.3 uH (compact / low-inductance construction, not a large impulse hall).
